title: One unplaceable-reference rule replaces six reference lints
summary: This change collapses six separate reference rules (bare-reference, reference-without-label, reference-without-link, chat-local-reference, undefined-name, undefined-name-at-start) into a single `unplaceable-reference` rule backed by a new candidate engine in `crates/osf/src/lints/writing/reference.rs`. The engine finds numbers, phrases, times and names in a paragraph, then decides whether the paragraph itself places each one — a link, a bracketed description, a named repository, a file path, a known name, a definer sentence, an absolute date. Anything left unplaced becomes a finding. Alongside it, `osf-lint-core::resolve` gains an `Evidence` argument: statistical evidence (a capitalised name guessed from shape, a quoted lowercase term) always resolves to Warning/Advise in every context, so a guess can never refuse a reply. A 68-fixture corpus plus a precision/recall measure and end-to-end hook tests pin the new rule's behaviour.

lanes.label: Callers
lanes.subtitle: hooks, CLI, scan
lanes.summary: Entry points that hand text to the writing lint and act on the findings it returns.

lanes.label: Lint core
lanes.subtitle: osf-lint-core
lanes.summary: Shared rule metadata, context and the level/remediation resolver every caller goes through.

lanes.label: Writing lint
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/lints/writing
lanes.summary: The rule set that reads a document and produces findings, including the new candidate engine.

lanes.label: Fixtures and measures
lanes.subtitle: tests
lanes.summary: The corpus and the tests that pin precision, recall and end-to-end behaviour.

nodes.label: Stop hook
nodes.subtitle: hook.rs stop_with_input
nodes.summary: Reads the assistant's last message from stdin and refuses the turn (exit 2) when a blocking finding is present. A new test proves a reply whose only finding is a weak-evidence name is not refused.

nodes.label: Prompt hook
nodes.subtitle: hook prompt
nodes.summary: Prints the reminder text on every prompt. A new end-to-end test asserts it never names one of the six retired rule ids.

nodes.label: Commit-message check
nodes.subtitle: osf lint writing --context commit
nodes.summary: Lints a commit message file. The same relative time that a transcript may use fails here, which the new checkpoint test exercises.

nodes.label: Scan resolve_and_explain
nodes.subtitle: scan/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves each scan finding's level and remediation, now passing the finding's own evidence into the shared resolver.

nodes.label: resolve()
nodes.subtitle: class, group, context, exception, evidence
nodes.summary: The single decision point for level and remediation. A new first branch returns Warning/Advise for any statistical evidence, before the transcript and class/group logic runs.

nodes.label: Evidence
nodes.subtitle: Deterministic | Statistical
nodes.summary: Marks whether a finding rests on a fact or a guess. Statistical findings can never block, whatever the rule's class, group or exception says.

nodes.label: RuleMeta::resolve
nodes.subtitle: writing/meta.rs
nodes.summary: Forwards the caller's evidence to the shared resolver. The new unplaceable-reference rule's doc text is registered here.

nodes.label: lint_writing
nodes.subtitle: writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Runs the rule set over a document. Now calls unplaceable_reference between undefined_names and recap_ending, and passes each finding's evidence into resolution.

nodes.label: apply_context
nodes.subtitle: writing/mod.rs
nodes.summary: Resolves level and remediation per finding. Only unplaceable-reference forwards its own evidence; the older rules are pinned to Deterministic until they are retired.

nodes.label: unplaceable_reference
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: The new rule. Collects candidates per paragraph, keeps the first use of each name, picks one paragraph to report a repeated name from, and emits a finding for every candidate the paragraph does not place.

nodes.label: candidates()
nodes.subtitle: reference.rs
nodes.summary: Finds number, phrase, time and name candidates in one paragraph. Masks quoted and backticked spans first, then keeps the longest candidate per kind when two overlap.

nodes.label: number_candidates
nodes.subtitle: hash, word+number, word+(letter)
nodes.summary: Finds `#12`, `repo#125`, `issue 31` and `mechanism (b)`, excluding versions, years, ranges, units, measures, coordinates, known names and label-value list items.

nodes.label: phrase_candidates
nodes.subtitle: configured phrases, `above`
nodes.summary: Matches the configured chat-local phrases plus `the previous`, and decides whether `above` is a reference to earlier text or a preposition taking an object.

nodes.label: time_candidates
nodes.subtitle: ordinals, weekdays, relative days
nodes.summary: Finds bare ordinal days, weekdays and relative days. Relative days are skipped entirely in transcript context, since a reply is read in the moment it was sent.

nodes.label: name_candidates
nodes.subtitle: capitalised runs, quoted lowercase terms
nodes.summary: Finds capitalised runs with real evidence and lowercase double-quoted terms. Backticked spans are code and never yield a name.

nodes.label: is_placed
nodes.subtitle: rules.rs
nodes.summary: Decides whether the paragraph itself resolves a candidate: a link, a bracketed or colon description of two plain words, a named repository, a file path, a known name, a definer sentence, an absolute date.

nodes.label: KnownNames
nodes.subtitle: built-in list + project file
nodes.summary: The list a name is checked against. New built-ins cover frameworks and model tiers (React, Vite, Tauri, RFC, Sonnet, Opus, Haiku), and a new is_generic_word helper lets a caller treat any other known name as a real name.

nodes.label: unplaceable fixtures
nodes.subtitle: 68 markdown cases
nodes.summary: Each fixture carries an osf-unplaceable header naming its label, kind, target and reason. Placeable cases must not fire; unplaceable cases must.

nodes.label: unplaceable_measure
nodes.subtitle: precision and recall table
nodes.summary: Runs the lint over every fixture and requires 100% precision and recall per kind, with no finding landing away from its own target.

nodes.label: unplaceable_checkpoints
nodes.subtitle: end-to-end hook and CLI
nodes.summary: Drives the compiled binary through the stop hook, the commit-message check and the prompt hook, proving the rule fires and refuses where it should and never names a retired rule id.

edges.label: last assistant message
edges.summary: The stop hook lints the reply before deciding whether to refuse the turn.

edges.label: commit message
edges.summary: The commit-message check lints the message file in commit context.

edges.label: doc, known, cfg, context
edges.summary: The new rule is wired into the writing lint between undefined_names and recap_ending.

edges.label: one paragraph at a time
edges.summary: The rule asks the candidate engine for every candidate in each paragraph.
Number candidates are collected first, against the quote-masked text.
Phrase candidates come from the configured list plus the `above` analysis.
Time candidates depend on the context, since a transcript skips relative days.
Name candidates read the quoted spans and the document-wide run counts.

edges.label: candidate + paragraph
edges.summary: Each candidate is tested against the paragraph that contains it.

edges.label: known name lookup
edges.summary: A name is placed when it is on the known-names list, word by word or by a known head word.
Findings are resolved per context after the rules have run.

edges.label: context + evidence
edges.summary: Only unplaceable-reference forwards its own evidence; the older rules stay Deterministic.
RuleMeta::resolve now takes an evidence argument and forwards it.
The scan path also passes the finding's evidence into the shared resolver.

edges.label: Statistical → Warning/Advise
edges.summary: The new first branch: statistical evidence always resolves to Warning and Advise, before any class, group, context or exception logic.
The measure runs the lint over every fixture and asserts perfect precision and recall.
Each fixture's header supplies the label, kind and target the measure scores against.
The checkpoint test spawns the real binary and feeds it a stop event on stdin.
The checkpoint test writes a commit message file and runs the lint subcommand over it.
The checkpoint test asserts the prompt reminder never names a retired rule id.

flows.title: From paragraph text to a placed or unplaced finding
flows.summary: One paragraph enters the candidate engine, which masks quoted spans and collects number, phrase, time and name candidates. The rule then asks is_placed about each candidate; anything the paragraph does not resolve becomes a finding, and the finding's evidence decides whether it can block.

sample.text: Deploying fix 5 cleared the stuck queue.

response.shape: kind: Number | Phrase | Time | Name, text, range

messages.label: candidate + paragraph + known
messages.note: A number is placed by a link, a bracketed or colon description of two plain words, a named repository, a file path, or a bracketed letter with a matching list item. A name is placed by the known-names list or a definer sentence.

messages.label: Finding { rule: unplaceable-reference, evidence }
messages.note: A weak-evidence name and a quoted lowercase term carry Evidence::Statistical; every other candidate carries Deterministic.

response.shape: rule, level, remediation, excerpt, message, evidence

messages.label: class, group, context, exception, evidence
messages.note: Statistical evidence short-circuits to Warning/Advise before the transcript and class/group logic runs, so a guess can never refuse a reply.
